extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and eligibility requirements, examiner guidance, and applicant obligations for accelerated and Track One (prioritized) examination programs, plus rules on suspension of action and refunds under MPEP §708–709.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canceled Elected Claims, Non-Responsive — Accelerated Examination (¶8.26.AE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to a non-elected invention is non-responsive (MPEP § 821.03). Since the amendment appears to be a bona fide attempt to reply, applicant is given a shortened statutory period of TWO (2) MONTHS from the mailing date of this notice to supply the omission or correction to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application has been granted special status under the accelerated examination program. Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available, but filing a petition for extension of time will result in the application being taken out of the accelerated examination program. In no case can any extension carry the date for reply beyond the maximum period of SIX MONTHS set by statute (35 U.S.C. 133). To meet the program objective (complete examination within 12 months), any reply must be filed electronically via the USPTO patent electronic filing system; non-electronic replies may delay final disposition beyond 12 months. Examiner note: this form paragraph may only be used in applications filed on or after August 25, 2006 that have been granted special status under the accelerated examination program or under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(2) or (d); it should not be used for applications granted special status under 1.102(c)(1) (health/age) or the Patent Prosecution Highway pilot program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for Information — Accelerated Examination (¶19.02.AE)
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest under 37 CFR 1.291 has been considered and additional information from applicant is necessary; the failure to reply to this requirement for information within TWO (2) MONTHS will result in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application has been granted special status under the accelerated examination program. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are available but filing a petition for extension will remove the application from the accelerated program; no extension can carry the reply date beyond the six-month statutory maximum (35 U.S.C. 133). Replies must be filed electronically to meet the 12-month objective; non-electronic replies may cause final disposition to occur later than 12 months. Examiner note: use only for applications filed on or after August 25, 2006 and having accelerated status per 1.102(c)(2) or (d); not for health/age special status or PPH pilot program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability Restrictions for Accelerated/Prioritized Form Paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain form paragraphs and the accelerated examination procedures may only be used for applications filed on or after August 25, 2006 and that have been granted special status under the accelerated examination program or on other grounds under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(2) or (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use these form paragraphs for applications granted special status under 37 CFR 1.102(c)(1) (health or age) or the Patent Prosecution Highway pilot program. Examiner notes repeat these applicability limitations to prevent misuse of the form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized Examination — General (37 CFR 1.102(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for prioritized examination must comply with 37 CFR 1.102(e) and be accompanied by the prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)), the processing fee (1.17(i)), and, if not already paid, the publication fee (1.18(d)). An application for which prioritized examination is requested may not contain or be amended to contain more than four independent claims, more than thirty total claims, or any multiple dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritized examination will not be accorded to international applications not in the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, design applications, reissue applications, provisional applications, or reexamination proceedings. No more than 15,000 requests will be accepted per fiscal year. A request must also meet specific requirements for either newly filed applications (Track One) or RCEs (PE-RCE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized Examination — Type of Application Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be a utility or plant nonprovisional application, including a continuing application (continuation, CIP, or divisional). The procedure does not apply to design, reissue, provisional applications, or reexamination proceedings; international applications that have entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371 are generally not eligible except when associated with an RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continuing application is not automatically given prioritized status based on the parent application; each application must independently meet 37 CFR 1.102(e) requirements. A utility or plant nonprovisional filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) may claim priority to a foreign application and remain eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized Examination — Required Fees on Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon filing the request for prioritized examination, the following fees must be paid: (A) prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)); (B) processing fee (1.17(i)(1)); (C) publication fee (1.18(d)); (D) basic filing fee (1.16(a)) or plant basic filing (1.16(c)); (E) search fee (1.16(k)) or plant search fee (1.16(m)); and (F) examination fee (1.16(o)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small and micro entity fee reductions may apply. If any fee is unpaid at filing, the request will be dismissed unless explicit authorization to charge required fees is provided in the papers. If a fee is set to $0 by the USPTO, it is considered paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized Examination — Claims Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must contain, or be amended to contain, no more than four independent claims and no more than thirty total claims, and must not contain any multiple dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After prioritized examination is granted, an amendment resulting in more than four independent claims, more than thirty total claims, or a multiple dependent claim will terminate prioritized examination. If the application does not meet the claim limit when the request is considered, the decision will provide one month to amend claims consistent with the requirements; that one-month period is not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized Examination — Yearly Cap and System Notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of granted requests for prioritized examination is limited to a maximum of 15,000 per fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office posts statistics on the number granted and will post a message in the USPTO patent electronic filing system if/when the number of granted requests is close to the limit. If limit reached, the Office will disable the ability to file a request for prioritized examination in Patent Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized Examination — Recommended Filing Practices and Form PTO/AIA/424
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly recommended that applicants use the Office's certification and request form PTO/AIA/424 to request prioritized examination, though the form is not strictly required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to use the form could result in the Office not recognizing the request or processing delays. Any item submitted on the same day the request is filed will be considered filed with the request. If applicant uses an applicant-created form, it should be equivalent to the Office form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track One (New Application) — Additional Filing Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain Track One prioritized examination for a newly filed 35 U.S.C. 111(a) application, the application must include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 with at least one claim, a drawing when necessary, and an inventor's oath or declaration or an application data sheet meeting 1.53(f)(3)(i). Utility applications must be filed via the USPTO patent electronic filing system; plant applications must be filed in paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be filed on or after Sep 26, 2011 to be eligible as Track One. Filing must include required filing/search/examination fees; any excess claims/size fees due must be paid before Track One status is granted. A nonpublication request may be submitted but the publication fee still must be paid when requesting prioritized examination (refund may be requested later if not published). Color drawings permitted but petition required for entry of color. If required items omitted, follow-on submissions are allowed only if submitted the same day as filing of the application and prioritized request; only registered Patent Center users can submit such follow-on documents electronically on the same day.

rubrics_metrics.name: PE-RCE (Prioritized Examination for RCE) — Eligibility and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A pending non-reissue utility or plant nonprovisional application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), or an application that has entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, may be granted PE-RCE status if conditions are met. The PE-RCE request must be filed before the mailing of the first Office action after the filing of the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publication fee (1.18(d)) must be paid previously or with the prioritized request. Prosecution must be closed (under appeal, final office action, notice of allowance, or otherwise closed) before filing the RCE. Only a single PE-RCE request may be granted in an application. Prioritized examination will not be granted where the RCE does not meet 37 CFR 1.114 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximizing Benefit of Prioritized Examination (Applicant Recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: To maximize the benefit of prioritized examination, applicants should: (A) acquire a good knowledge of the state of the prior art to file a clear specification with a complete schedule of claims from broadest to narrowest; (B) submit an application in condition for examination; (C) file replies that are completely responsive to Office actions and within the shortened statutory period; and (D) be prepared to conduct interviews with the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'in condition for examination' is the same as used for accelerated examination (see MPEP §708.02(a) subsection VIII.C). These practices help the Office meet its goal of final disposition within 12 months on average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution Under Prioritized Examination — Time Periods and Termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Time periods set for reply in Office actions for prioritized applications are the same as set forth in MPEP §710.02(b). Filing a petition for an extension of time or a request for suspension of action will terminate prioritized examination. An amendment resulting in >4 independent claims, >30 total claims, or a multiple dependent claim will terminate prioritized examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon termination, the application is removed from the examiner's special docket and placed on the examiner's regular docket. The Office's goal is final disposition within twelve months, on average, of the date prioritized status was granted; 'final disposition' means mailing of notice of allowance, mailing of a final Office action, filing of a notice of appeal, completion of examination per 37 CFR 41.102, filing of an RCE, or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of Fees for Prioritized Examination Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for prioritized examination is dismissed, the prioritized examination fee (37 CFR 1.17(c)) will be refunded automatically (if paid). The processing fee (1.17(i)) will be retained to cover processing costs. Application fees (basic filing, search, examination, and any required application size or excess claim fees) cannot be refunded under 37 CFR 1.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may request a refund of the search fee and any excess claims fees by filing a petition for express abandonment under 37 CFR 1.138(d). Applicant may request refund of the publication fee per MPEP §1126 if the application is not published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b). Termination of prioritized examination does not entitle applicant to a refund of the prioritized examination fee on the grounds that prioritized examination was terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) — Program Purpose and Use
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPH speeds up examination for corresponding applications filed in participating patent offices. When an applicant receives a final ruling from a first patent office that at least one claim is allowed, the applicant may request fast track examination of corresponding claims in a pending corresponding application in a second patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH leverages fast-track procedures among participating offices to reach final disposition more quickly. The USPTO participates in Global PPH and IP5 PPH pilot programs and has bilateral PPH agreements; details and forms are on the USPTO PPH webpage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of Action — General (37 CFR 1.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of the applicant, the Office may grant suspension of action for good and sufficient cause. The Office will not suspend action if a reply by applicant to an Office action is outstanding. Petitions must specify a period not exceeding six months and include the fee set forth in 1.17(g) unless the cause is the fault of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension under 1.103 applies to impending Office action by the examiner and should not be confused with extension of time for reply (37 CFR 1.136), which applies to applicant action. Suspension reduces any patent term adjustment accumulated under 37 CFR 1.703 by the number of days of suspension per 1.704(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited Suspension in CPA or After RCE (37 CFR 1.103(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited suspension of action in a CPA filed under 1.53(d) may be granted for up to three months (request must be filed with the CPA and include processing fee 1.17(i)). Limited suspension after filing an RCE under 1.114 may be granted for up to three months if filed with the RCE and including processing fee 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request for suspension of action under these paragraphs must specify the period and include the processing fee. Such suspensions also affect patent term adjustment as noted for general suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of Examination (37 CFR 1.103(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of the applicant, the Office may grant deferral of examination for a period not extending beyond three years from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is claimed under Title 35, provided conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A deferral request must include the publication fee (1.18(d)) and processing fee (1.17(i)). The deferral will not be granted unless: (1) application is an original utility or plant application filed under 1.53(b) or from national stage (1.495); (2) the applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under 1.213(a) (or has rescinded it); (3) the application is in condition for publication as provided in 1.211(c); and (4) the Office has not issued either an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Suspension on Initiative of the Office; Suspension for Public Safety or Defense
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will notify applicant if it suspends action on its own initiative. The Director may suspend action if (1) the application is owned by the United States, (2) publication may be detrimental to public safety or defense, and (3) the appropriate department or agency requests such suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These suspensions are distinct from applicant-requested suspensions and have specific national-security/public-safety bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition Under 37 CFR 1.103(a) — Required Contents and Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for suspension under 1.103(a) must be presented as a separate paper, be accompanied by the petition fee (1.17(g)), request a specific and reasonable suspension period not greater than six months, and present good and sufficient reasons why the suspension is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing of good and sufficient cause should specifically explain what factors directly impact the applicant's ability to presently prosecute the application. A statement referring only to general circumstances (e.g., 'global pandemic') may not suffice. If requirements are met, suspension begins on the day the request is filed; otherwise the application will be taken up for action in normal order.
